claim: Elastic net models that use several quarters of standardized unexpected earnings (SUE) history forecast returns better than one-quarter SUE or streak features: models with up to 12 quarters beat shorter-horizon and streak-based approaches in returns, Sharpe ratio and alpha; Sharpe ratios nearly double, alphas stay significant after controlling for one-quarter SUE and streak effects; gains are strongest among large caps, where the latest surprise is priced quickly but older surprises are overlooked.
quote: Gains are especially strong among large-cap stocks, where the latest surprises are quickly priced in but older ones remain overlooked.
market_and_period: US equities, sample period, universe, label, cost treatment and post-2020 results NOT readable (full text blocked).
applicability: Defines the tested design: multi-quarter SUE history -> elastic net -> long-short/long portfolio; large-cap emphasis motivates the S&P 500 pool.
limitations: Only the abstract could be read: features beyond 'up to 12 quarters of SUE' (revenue surprise? streak count definition?), label horizon, out-of-sample design, costs and reported Sharpe are unknown. Paper's SUE is built from announcement-date data (Compustat/IBES style); ours is visible only at the 10-Q/10-K filing date, which lags the earnings press release, so the announcement-day reaction is missed and PEAD measured here is post-filing drift.
independent_replication: No independent replication found. Subrahmanyam (2025, see UCLA Anderson Review item) contests 2025 PEAD-revival papers on microcap grounds (different papers).
verification_method: WebFetch/WebSearch summary, full text not available
impact_on_spec: Shapes candidate set, baselines and caveats in candidate-manifest.json.

applicability: Prior against any PEAD signal in the S&P 500 pool; the multi-quarter idea must beat this by using older, not latest, surprises.
limitations: Abstract only; tests the last-quarter surprise, not multi-quarter history.
independent_replication: Contradicted in part by two 2025 papers (Dickerson-Julliard-Mueller JFE forthcoming; Hirshleifer-Peng-Wang RFS 2025) per the UCLA Anderson Review item.
